description: baseline: unmodified design (rho=1 LQR, kf qa=qd=1), run via frozen measure.sh through local Bash (see charter protocol note)

asi.hypothesis: lower qd smooths d-hat propagation during degraded GNSS, reducing estimate jitter; RMS slightly worse but re-acquisition transient (max, tilt) clearly reduced
asi.next_action_hint: structural: blend Lb->Lg softly at RTK re-acquisition in kf_sfun (ramp over ~1 s) to attack the 0.615 m peak + 27° tilt directly; also try qa sweep later

description: exp2: kf qd 1.0 -> 0.3 (smoother d-hat during outage)

asi.hypothesis: Lb->Lg 1.5 s ramp after re-acquisition smooths the estimate jump; RMS improved 0.41% but peak/tilt identical => transient happens DURING the outage, not at re-acquisition
asi.next_action_hint: attack the outage itself: Lb structure / qd tuning (qd=0.3 earlier cut peak 5% & tilt 2.6 deg but hurt RMS slightly); try qd=0.5 with ramp kept, or scale down Lb position rows

description: exp3: kf_sfun soft re-acquisition (1.5 s Lb->Lg gain ramp, extra ts state)

asi.hypothesis: intermediate qd=0.5 keeps some peak/tilt gain without the qd=0.3 RMS penalty — refuted: RMS worse (+0.8%) and ewind also worse (0.0791->0.0813); qd trades d-hat gust-following speed for smoothness, RMS-optimal is near qd=1.0
asi.next_action_hint: stop tuning qd (direction exhausted); try qa=0.5 (smoother v-hat during outage, good-fix phases dominated by small Rg so barely affected), then lb_scale<1 in kf_design (trust degraded GNSS less)
asi.rollback: revisit qd<1 only if the objective switches to minimizing peak/tilt (separate segment) — peak 0.607 / tilt 25.6 deg clearly better there

description: exp4: qd 1.0 -> 0.5 on top of kept re-acquisition ramp

asi.hypothesis: qa=0.5 smooths v-hat under noisy position updates during outage — refuted hard: RMS +3.2%, peak worse; sluggish v-hat slows drift correction (est_p did improve 0.054 vs 0.056 but tracking suffers)
asi.next_action_hint: stop tuning qa downward; next: P.kf.lb_scale=0.5 in kf_design (scale degraded-gain Lb, trust 0.5 m-noise GNSS less during outage); opposite probe qa=2.0 only if lb_scale fails
asi.rollback: qa<1 hurts both RMS and peak; qa>1 untested but low expected value given v-hat already fast at qa=1

description: exp5: kf qa 1.0 -> 0.5 (slower v-hat correction)

asi.hypothesis: scaling Lb down (trust degraded GNSS less) reduces noise-driven drift — refuted hard: RMS +13.5%, peak 0.704; position updates during outage still help even at sigma=0.5 m. ARE optimum for Rb is already lb_scale=1
asi.next_action_hint: degraded-gain direction exhausted (0.5 tested worse; >1 injects more noise — no path). Segment plateau confirmed across qa/qd/lb_scale/ramp; summarize or open a new segment for LQR weight scaling (lower expected value: outage error is drift-dominated, not noise-reaction)
asi.rollback: don't revisit Lb scaling unless outage GNSS sigma assumption changes (e.g. sensor spec revision)

description: exp6: degraded-fix gain Lb scaled x0.5 in kf_design

asi.hypothesis: matching the disturbance model to the true gust dynamics (OU tau=2) + slow RW bias improves outage prediction — marginally confirmed: ertk_rms -0.07%, ewind -0.07%; dominant outage error is GNSS noise passthrough, not drift, so d-model gains are small
asi.next_action_hint: one qf probe (0.5 or 0.1) to confirm the matched value is optimal; beyond that the remaining lever is certainty-equivalence: fix-aware LQR gain scaling (needs ctrl_sfun input port + model rewiring, charter says avoid)
asi.rollback: keep regardless: physically-correct model, strictly better on both primary and ewind; if qf sweep finds better value, keep that too
